Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant and perused the record.
In the FIR, it is alleged that the daughter of the informant Mahi Gupta (deceased) was married to one Pankaj Gupta son of the present applicant on 03.05.2022 according to Hindu Rights and Rituals.
After the marriage, one Bullet Motorcycle and Rs.50000/- cash was demanded by the named accused persons.
The daughter of the informant told on telephone regarding demand of dowry, upon that the informant went to the place of her daughter and settled the matter.
It has been further alleged that the deceased was three months' pregnant and the son-in-law of the informant as Pankaj Gupta vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home U.P. ...

well as father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased were not willing to born the child and they were pressuring the deceased for the abortion.
On 24.09.2023 at 10:20 AM, he received information that the deceased has died.
When the informant reached there, he saw that the deceased suffered antemortem injuries.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant having no criminal history is languishing in jail since 27.09.2023.
Three prosecution witnesses have been examined before the trial court.
PW-2 and 3 have been declared hostile.

He further submits that except the ligature mark,
there is no antemortem injury on the body of the deceased.
Cause of death is asphyxia as a result of antemortem hanging.
It has been further submitted that by making general allegations six family members of the applicant have falsely been implicated.
There is no specific statement of the prosecution witnesses as to when the demand of dowry was made or cruelty was committed upon the deceased.
Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that perusal of the site plan shows that the deceased committed suicide in her room on the second floor.
It is further submitted that the information of the incident was given by the applicant to his in laws.
There is no possibility of the applicant of fleeing away after being released from jail or tampering with the witnesses.
In case the applicant is enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.
Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail and submits that the victim has died within three months of the marriage.

On due consideration to the fact that three fact witnesses including the complainant have been examined before the trial court; except the ligature mark, there is no antemortem injury on the body of the deceased, the applicant is languishing in jail since 27.09.2023 without having any criminal antecedent and the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Javed Gulam Nabi Shaikh vs.
State of Maharashtra (2024) 9 SCC 813, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Act, Police Station - Mohammadi, District Kheri, be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
